model: claude-opus-5-5 (session model) for writers, checkers and rewrites

problems: q12 lists the components in the same order as the key ("the replica, the API servers, replica reads and DNS"), so the order can be guessed from the question alone; reword it neutrally, for example "in what order are the region's components (DNS, replica reads, API servers, replica) brought up", or just ask for the bring-up sequence.

q6 ("Which reads go to the primary regardless of the user's region or the replica's health?") also fits rule (d) in the reference, because pinned users' reads go to the primary in any region whatever the replica's health, so a correct reader could answer with pinned reads instead of the key; reword it to ask which endpoints or pages always read from the primary, even during a primary outage.
seeded_presentation never says that geo-DNS routes by client IP, which is part of the q2 key, so that part of the answer is not recoverable; add "by client IP" to its item 1.

The reference's Part A heading says the shared pieces "ship to all three regions first", but no API servers exist in eu-west-1 or ap-southeast-1 until steps 8 and 11, which could mislead a reader on q12's ordering; reword it to say the shared code ships in the API build and to the primary and us-east-1 before any per-region work.

The reference checks lag only every 1 s and trips at more than 5 s, so a replica can keep serving for up to about 1 s after it passes the 5 s limit, which goes against the brief's hard "must not serve reads" rule; either make the check trip below 5 s (for example at 4 s) or state the detection window explicitly.
first_problems: Requirement r3 adds 'The plan says how lag is measured', but the brief never asks for this, which breaks rule 9; drop that sentence from r3 and leave lag measurement to design item q8.

reference_artifact never says that a write is synchronous and must commit on the primary before the API responds, or that any commit failure (including one in the roughly 3 s before primary_up flips) returns an error to the user; q1's key ('synchronously ... if it cannot commit, the user gets an error') and r1 ('commit there before the response') are only implied, so add that sentence to router rule (a).

reference_artifact does not follow the brief's per-step format ('what starts it, what data moves, where any state lives, and what happens when it fails') for steps 3, 5, 7, 8, 9 and 11; for example, it gives no failure handling for a replica that never meets the 1-hour catch-up gate or for failed smoke tests, so add those fields to each step.

q10's key includes 'new instances start with the replica marked not ok', which the question (recovery after lag removal) does not ask for; remove it from the key or widen the question to cover instance start-up state.

q11's key includes write behaviour ('Writes then get 503 without being tried') and recovery ('One successful check sets primary_up back to true'), which the question (detection and read routing) does not ask for; trim the key or add those parts to the question so graders do not mark complete answers as partial.

The 'what gates user traffic' half of q12 is already settled by the brief ('no user traffic until its replica is less than 5 seconds behind'), so the design item is partly a brief item; narrow it to the order of steps within a region and how catch-up is confirmed (for example, how long lag must stay under 5 s).

reference_artifact contradicts itself: step 8 says that with replica_reads off 'all of their reads and writes go to the primary', but router rule (c) comes before rule (e), so during a primary outage reads would go to the local replica even with replica_reads off; make rule (c) apply only when replica_reads is on, or state the exception in step 8.

seeded_implicit's line 'A primary outage is handled by the existing runbook' can be read as false, because the reference handles an outage automatically (writes return 503, new regions serve stale replica reads) and only failover is manual; reword it to 'Primary failover stays on the existing manual runbook.'

problems: Section 3 of reference_artifact (and the same text in seeded_presentation) says an unset app.tenant_id reads as NULL. That stops being true once a pooled connection has run set_config('app.tenant_id', ..., true): in later transactions current_setting('app.tenant_id', true) returns '' and ''::uuid raises an error. So on a reused PgBouncer connection a no-tenant query errors instead of returning zero rows, and the login transaction that sets only app.user_id fails when it reads memberships (the q7 flow). Fix: use NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '')::uuid, and the same for app.user_id, in both policies.

Section 3 of reference_artifact and the q1 key both say updates are rejected when no tenant is set. Under the stated USING/WITH CHECK tenant policy, an UPDATE or DELETE just matches zero rows and raises no error; only an INSERT fails WITH CHECK. A plan that describes this correctly would be marked wrong against the q1 key. Fix: reword the q1 key in the brief's own terms (sees no rows, writes cannot change anything) and correct the reference, or add a mechanism that really makes updates and deletes fail.

The login policy on memberships in reference_artifact (user_id = app.user_id, FOR SELECT) applies in every transaction, and every tenant request also sets app.user_id. So inside tenant A's context the user also sees their own membership rows in other tenants, which is wider than the brief's exception (listing memberships only before choosing a tenant). Fix: add a condition that no tenant is set (for example NULLIF(current_setting('app.tenant_id', true), '') IS NULL), or say plainly that this wider visibility is intended.
first_problems: The brief says a query run with no tenant selected must see nothing, and r3 and the q1 key repeat this, but the reference's login policy lets a query with only app.user_id set read the user's own memberships in every tenant; the reference therefore breaks a fixed requirement, and a candidate who follows the brief literally has no valid answer to q7. Fix it by adding a plain carve-out to the brief, r3 and the q1 key (for example: a user may list their own memberships before choosing a tenant, without saying how), or by changing how the reference handles tenant selection.

The brief's list of tenant-owned data (projects, tasks, comments, guest access, audit events) leaves out memberships, so it is unclear whether memberships are tenant-owned and under RLS; the reference, r2 and q7 all assume they are. State in the brief that memberships belong to exactly one tenant.

q9 ('What in the schema makes that removal outcome happen automatically when the membership is deleted?') assumes the reference's mechanism, so a valid design that soft-deletes memberships or unassigns tasks inside the removal transaction cannot answer it. Reword it to ask what mechanism unassigns the person's tasks and keeps their comments, and what the task assignee and the comment author each reference.

The q11 key says 'audit events have no FK', but the reference gives audit_events foreign keys to tenants (tenant_id) and to users (actor_user_id). Change the key to 'audit events have no FK to projects or tasks'.
